facts.statement: Allodaposuchus lived in southern Europe during the Campanian and Maastrichtian stages of the Late Cretaceous, and possibly the Santonian stage.
facts.quote: Allodaposuchus is an extinct genus of crocodyliforms that lived in what is now southern Europe during the Campanian and Maastrichtian stages, and possibly the Santonian stage, of the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Fossils of Allodaposuchus are known from Romania, Spain, and France.
facts.quote: Allodaposuchus is one of the most common Late Cretaceous crocodylomorphs from Europe, with fossils known from Romania, Spain, and France.

facts.statement: The largest known specimen of Allodaposuchus was probably around 3 meters long.
facts.quote: The largest known specimen of Allodaposuchus belongs to an individual that was probably around 3 m long.

facts.statement: The species A. precedens has been estimated to be 7 meters (23 feet) long.
facts.quote: A.precedens has been estimated at 7 m (23 ft) long.

facts.statement: Allodaposuchus generally had a short, flattened, and rounded skull.
facts.quote: Allodaposuchus has a short, flattened, and rounded skull.

facts.statement: A. hulki possessed large, unique skull sinuses that may have aided hearing out of water and lightened the skull.
facts.quote: A. hulki has large sinuses in its skull that are not seen in any other crocodylian living or extinct and may have aided it in hearing out of water, as well as lightening the skull.

facts.statement: A. hulki had well-developed muscle attachments on its forelimb bones that would have allowed a semi-erect stance suitable for walking on land.
facts.quote: Moreover, A. hulki has well-developed muscle attachments on its scapula, humerus, and ulna bones that would have allowed the forelimbs to have been held in a semi-erect stance suitable for walking over land.

facts.statement: Remains of A. hulki were found in sediments likely formed in ephemeral ponds within a large floodplain far from permanent water bodies.
facts.quote: Remains of A. hulki come from interbedded sandstones and marls that, based on the presence of charophyte algae, likely formed in ephemeral ponds in a large floodplain far from permanent bodies of water like lakes or rivers.

facts.statement: The species A. hulki is named after the Marvel Comics character Hulk due to bone features suggesting strong muscles.
facts.quote: The species is named after the Hulk from Marvel Comics, in reference to features on the bones that suggest it had strong muscles.

facts.statement: The type species A. precedens was named by Franz Nopcsa in 1928 from fossils found in Vălioara, Romania.
facts.quote: The type species of Allodaposuchus, A. precedens, was named by Hungarian paleontologist Franz Nopcsa in 1928 from Vălioara, Romania.

facts.statement: The original fossils of A. precedens were found in the Hațeg Basin dating to the late Maastrichtian stage.
facts.quote: Nopcsa found bone fragments in a deposit of the Hațeg Basin that dates back to the late Maastrichtian stage – the very end of the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Fossils of A. precedens from Campanian-age deposits suggest the species persisted for about 5 million years.
facts.quote: Some of these skulls came from Campanian-age deposits slightly older than those in Romania, meaning that the species must have persisted for about 5 million years.

facts.statement: A neotype for Allodaposuchus was designated in 2020 after a petition approved by the ICZN in 2017.
facts.quote: A petition to designate the specimen PSMUBB V 438 as the neotype to replace the original non-diagnostic type specimen was submitted to the International Commission on Zoological Nomenclature (ICZN) in 2017, which was approved in 2020.

facts.statement: A. subjuniperus was named in 2013 based on a skull found in the Conquès Formation in Huesca, Spain.
facts.quote: In 2013, a second species of Allodaposuchus, A. subjuniperus, was named on the basis of a skull from the late-Maastrichtian Conquès Formation, part of the Tremp Group, in the province of Huesca, Spain.

facts.statement: The species name A. subjuniperus means "under juniper" because the skull was found beneath a juniper tree.
facts.quote: The skull was found underneath a juniper tree whose roots had grown between the bones, hence the species name subjuniperus or "under juniper" in Latin.

facts.statement: A. palustris was described in 2014 from fossils found in the Fumanya Sud locality in the southern Pyrenees.
facts.quote: In 2014, A. palustris was described from a partial skull and other skeletal fragments found in Maastrichtian age sediments of the Tremp Formation in a fossil locality called Fumanya Sud in the southern Pyrenees.

facts.statement: The fossils of A. palustris provided the first detailed description of the postcranial anatomy of Allodaposuchus.
facts.quote: These remains allowed for the first detailed description of the postcranial (non-skull) anatomy of Allodaposuchus.

facts.statement: A. hulki was named in 2015 from fossils found in the Casa Fabà locality within the Tremp Formation.
facts.quote: A fourth species of Allodaposuchus, A. hulki, was named in 2015 and also came from the Tremp Formation, although this time in a locality called Casa Fabà.

facts.statement: A species named A. iberoarmoricanus was described by Blanco in 2021 from fossils in Velaux-La Bastide Neuve, southern France.
facts.quote: A. palustris was described by Blanco in 2021 based on fossils discovered in Late Campanian-aged fluvial deposits in Velaux-La Bastide Neuve, in Bouches-du-Rhône Department of southern France.

facts.statement: Allodaposuchus is generally classified as a non-crocodylian eusuchian crocodylomorph but is sometimes placed among the earliest true crocodylians.
facts.quote: Although generally classified as a non-crocodylian eusuchian crocodylomorph, it is sometimes placed as one of the earliest true crocodylians.

facts.statement: Allodaposuchus belongs to the clade Allodaposuchidae.
facts.quote: Allodaposuchus belongs to the clade Allodaposuchidae.

facts.statement: The exact phylogenetic placement of Allodaposuchidae remains disputed among researchers.
facts.quote: The exact placement of Allodaposuchidae is still in dispute.

facts.statement: There is a debate regarding whether Allodaposuchidae is the sister group to Hylaeochampsidae or represents an evolutionary grade towards Crocodylia.
facts.quote: Narváez et al. considered it the sister group to Hylaeochampsidae, which together form a clade that is sister to Crocodylia. Other studies have alternatively recovered them not as sister taxon, but rather as an evolutionary grade towards Crocodylia, with Hylaeochampsidae more basal than Allodaposuchidae.

facts.statement: A 2021 analysis suggested that Allodaposuchidae belongs within Crocodylia.
facts.quote: Alternatively, a 2021 analysis incorporating postcranial information recovered Allodaposuchidae within Crocodylia.

facts.statement: A 2021 study proposed that Agaresuchus and Lohuecosuchus are junior synonyms of Allodaposuchus, making the genus paraphyletic.
facts.quote: In the 2021 study, Blanco recovered Allodaposuchus as paraphyletic, with Agaresuchus and Lohuecosuchus. Accordingly, Blanco proposed that Agaresuchus and Lohuecosuchus should be considered junior synonyms of Allodaposuchus.

facts.statement: The precise membership of the genus Allodaposuchus is currently disputed.
facts.quote: While there are several described species of Allodaposuchus, the precise membership of the group is currently disputed.

facts.statement: Some studies have suggested that Allodaposuchus is a nomen dubium because the original material is too fragmentary.
facts.quote: A study published in 2005 had suggested that these fossils belong to several different genera of crocodylomorphs and that the original Romanian material is too fragmentary to assign to its own genus, making Allodaposuchus a nomen dubium or "dubious name".

facts.statement: In 2016, A. subjuniperus was moved to the genus Agaresuchus because researchers considered it distinct from A. precedens.
facts.quote: However, in 2016, A. subjuniperus was moved to a new genus, Agaresuchus along with the type species of that genus, A. fontisensis, on the grounds that the Spanish species were sufficiently distinct from A. precedens.

facts.statement: Blanco's 2021 study questioned the separation of Agaresuchus and proposed it be treated as a junior synonym of Allodaposuchus.
facts.quote: However, Blanco's 2021 study has called this into question, and instead proposed that they should both be considered members of Allodaposuchus, with Agaresuchus as a junior synonym.

facts.statement: Blanco's 2021 study proposed that Lohuecosuchus be treated as a junior synonym of Allodaposuchus.
facts.quote: However, Blanco's 2021 study has called this into question, and instead proposed that they should both be considered members of Allodaposuchus, with Lohuecosuchus as a junior synonym.

facts.statement: The largest known specimen of Allodaposuchus was approximately 3.7 meters long.
facts.quote: El espécimen más grande de Allodaposuchus pertenece a un individuo que probablemente medía unos 3,7 metros de longitud.

facts.statement: Allodaposuchus had a short, flattened, and rounded skull.
facts.quote: Allodaposuchus tenía un cráneo corto, aplanado y redondeado.

facts.statement: A. hulki possessed large cranial sinuses not found in any other living or extinct crocodilian, which may have aided in hearing out of water and lightening the skull.
facts.quote: A. hulki tenía grandes senos en su cráneo que no se observan en ningún otro crocodiliano vivo o extinto y pudieron haberle ayudado a oír fuera del agua, así como a aligerar el cráneo.

facts.statement: A. hulki had well-developed muscle attachment points on its scapula, humerus, and cubitus that would allow it to maintain a semi-upright posture suitable for moving on land.
facts.quote: A. hulki tenía puntos de sujeción muscular bien desarrollados en su escápula, húmero y cúbito que le permitirían mantenerse en una postura semierguida apta para desplazarse sobre tierra.

facts.statement: The type species, A. precedens, was named by Hungarian paleontologist Franz Nopcsa in 1928 based on remains found in Vălioara, Romania.
facts.quote: La especie tipo de Allodaposuchus, A. precedens, fue nombrada por el paleontólogo húngaro Franz Nopcsa en 1928 de restos hallados en Vălioara, Rumania.

facts.statement: Fragments of A. precedens were found in the Hațeg Basin dating to the late Maastrichtian stage, just at the end of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Nopcsa halló fragmentos óseos en un depósito de la cuenca Hațeg que data de finales de la etapa del Maastrichtiense - justo al final del Cretácico Superior.

facts.statement: Some skulls of A. precedens come from Campanian-age deposits, suggesting the species persisted for nearly 5 million years.
facts.quote: Algunos de estos cráneos provienen de depósitos de edad campaniana, levemente más antiguos que los de Rumania, lo cual significa que la especie debe haber persistido por cerca de 5 millones de años.

facts.statement: A second species, A. subjuniperus, was named in 2013 based on a skull from the late Maastrichtian Conquès Formation in Huesca province, Spain.
facts.quote: En 2013 se nombró a una segunda especie de Allodaposuchus, A. subjuniperus, con base en un cráneo de finales del Maastrichtiense de la Formación Conqués en la provincia de Huesca, España.

facts.statement: The skull of A. subjuniperus was found under a juniper tree whose roots had grown among the bones, leading to the species name meaning "under the juniper" in Latin.
facts.quote: El cráneo fue hallado bajo un árbol de junípero cuyas raíces habían crecido entre los huesos, de aquí que el nombre de la especie subjuniperus signifique "bajo el junípero" en latín.

facts.statement: The third species, A. palustris, was described in 2014 based on material from an individual found in Fumanya, Barcelona, Spain, in Maastrichtian sediments of the Tremp Formation south of the Pyrenees.
facts.quote: En 2014 se describió la tercera especie del género, Allodaposuchus palustris, sobre la base de material perteneciente a un individuo hallado en Fumanya (Bergadá, Barcelona, España) en sedimentos del Maastrichtiense de la Formación Tremp al sur de los Pirineos.

facts.statement: A fourth species, A. hulki, was named in 2015 and also comes from the Tremp Formation, specifically from a locality called Casa Fabà.
facts.quote: Una cuarta especie de Allodaposuchus, A. hulki, fue nombrada en 2015 y también proviene de la Formación Tremp, aunque en este caso de una localidad llamada Casa Fabà.

facts.statement: The name A. hulki refers to the Marvel Comics character Hulk due to bone features suggesting it had strong muscles.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie es en referencia al personaje Hulk de Marvel Comics, debido a los rasgos de sus huesos que sugieren que tenía fuertes músculos.

facts.statement: Early phylogenetic studies concluded that Allodaposuchus was a close relative of modern crocodilians but excluded it from Crocodylia, the group including all modern crocodilians.
facts.quote: Los primeros estudios filogenéticos hechos para Allodaposuchus concluyeron en que era un pariente cercano de los crocodilianos modernos excluyéndolo de Crocodylia, el grupo que incluye a todos los crocodilianos modernos.

facts.statement: A 2010 phylogenetic analysis supported placing Allodaposuchus within Alligatoroidea, a group of crocodilians that includes modern alligators and Leidyosuchus.
facts.quote: Un análisis filogenético de 2010 apoyó una relación parecida a la clasificación de Nopsca de situar a Allodaposuchus dentro de Alligatoroidea, un grupo de crocodilianos que incluye a los actuales aligatores y a Leidyosuchus.

facts.statement: Inclusion of postcranial skeletal characters from A. palustris in a 2014 study supports a position within Crocodylia for the genus Allodaposuchus, separating it from Hylaeochampsidae.
facts.quote: La inclusión de los caracteres morfológicos observados en el esqueleto postcraneal de Allodaposuchus palustris en el estudio de 2014 apoyan una posición dentro de Crocodylia para el Género Allodaposuchus, separándolo de Hylaeochampsidae.

facts.statement: Allodaposuchus lived from the Santonian to the Maastrichtian, between 85.7 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Maastrichtian (85.7 to 66 million years ago)

facts.quote: Parent group: Allodaposuchidae

facts.statement: Allodaposuchus is classified in the family Allodaposuchidae.

facts.statement: Allodaposuchus is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.quote: Los restos de A. hulki provienen de areniscas y margas intercaladas que, basándose en la presencia de algas carofíceas, probablemente se formaban en charcas efímeras en grandes planicies de inundación lejos de los cuerpos de agua permanentes como los lagos o ríos.

facts.statement: Therefore, A. hulki may have spent most of its time out of water, traveling between these ponds in search of food.
facts.quote: Por tanto A. hulki puede haber pasado la mayor parte de su tiempo fuera del agua, viajando entre estas charcas en busca de comida.
